While everyone's talking about agents, I've been exploring how teams can use them to work better together.

Here’s my take, from OpenAI DevDay 2026.
My team wrote about how we run persistent agents inside OpenAI.
Would you enable yolo mode for dots, even if your dot might do sth unwanted?
There’s some new agent launching later this week and marketers offer a lot of money to say nice things about it on X. Keep a lookout on honest reviews 🫠
“Don't worry, you don't need to learn how to write this. Your agents will. And we made them really good at it.”
If that Spy’s goal was to destabilize one of the most successful American companies, they achieved their goal. Ousting Jensen feels rushed and not right.
reading some of these comments makes my brain hurt. oss is already hard enough without politics.

"When the company ran diagnostics on about 700 systems, it found 10,500 vulnerabilities and held an emergency press conference on June 16, applying fixes over three months.
However, when it re-ran diagnostics using "GPT-6 Astra," the latest model released by US-based OpenAI, it confirmed 35,000 new vulnerabilities. "Honestly, we're completely exhausted"

The Asahi project was all about taking something closed and restricted and opening it up.

Adding new restrictions that make it harder for other projects to build on that is not the way. And that AI rejection is just silly.

Is my perception off or is Apple just lying here? Anytime I build for or use Safari, it’s slower, has fewer features, weird bugs and plenty websites just don’t work. It’s a fight to get even somewhat close to Chrome’s performance.

Do individual limits still make sense? As capabilities increase you want to work with and support an agent that represents your project, that runs loops and evolves your codebase. The humans merely curate the automations.
This is smart. Wild that this wasn’t the default. Unpredictable inference quality was usually why I recommended skipping the middleman.
Another reason why you wanna use your own harness and not one where companies change what you can or can’t do at will.

Bullish on Andy Yen and Proton. He gets it.

The culture war, or rather the loss of identity some engineers feel as AI redefines our jobs is difficult; I sympathize. Also understand that he runs a business and might has limited patience when we now had two years to process, learn, change and grow.
Kinda funny how easy it is to spot bugs by agents vs humans. Someone at Disney still writes code by HAND?
I spent some time on the weekend to test bun's AOT compiler and results are nothing short of amazing. Performance up 2-3x, memory use less than half.
